docker_compose_file:
# Attested Vaultwarden on dstack (Intel TDX).
#
# Rendered by deploy/dstack/render.sh, which fills in the domain and the
# sidecar image digest and wraps the result into app-compose.json. dstack
# measures SHA-256(app-compose.json) into RTMR3 (`compose-hash`), so EVERY
# behaviour-affecting setting is literal here. Encrypted env values are not
# measured: the compose uses none (no variable interpolation). The only one a
# release may allow is GHCR_READ_TOKEN, read by the pre-launch script of the
# private-image variant (allowed_envs = ["GHCR_READ_TOKEN"], docs/PHALA.md 1b).
#
# TLS: the CVM's port 443 is exposed by the host as raw TCP (vmm `--port
# tcp:0.0.0.0:443:443`, or dstack-gateway TLS passthrough). Caddy generates
# the key inside the CVM and obtains the certificate with TLS-ALPN-01 from
# inside the CVM; the host only ever sees ciphertext.
name: attested-vaultwarden

services:
  vaultwarden:
    image: docker.io/vaultwarden/server@sha256:4fe17f415f90087377d37c755e0ea3cf189dcc6794e49cdd2a9adbb4937d9e1f # 1.37.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DOMAIN: "https://vault.facundo.dev"
      SIGNUPS_ALLOWED: "false"
      INVITATIONS_ALLOWED: "true"
      DISABLE_ICON_DOWNLOAD: "true"
      ICON_CACHE_TTL: "0"
      ICON_SERVICE: "internal"
      PUSH_ENABLED: "false"
      SSO_ENABLED: "false"
      PASSWORD_HINTS_ALLOWED: "false"
      SHOW_PASSWORD_HINT: "false"
      ORG_CREATION_USERS: "none"
      IP_HEADER: "X-Forwarded-For"
      LOG_LEVEL: "warn"
      # ADMIN_TOKEN deliberately unset: admin panel disabled (DECISIONS D-008).
      # SMTP not configured: invitations are accepted via the invite link.
      # Vaultwarden loads data/config.json at start and lets it OVERRIDE the
      # environment above (checked on 1.37.5). /data is persistent state that
      # the verifier cannot see, so a file planted there would change the
      # server's behaviour without changing any measurement. The config file
      # therefore lives on a tmpfs that is empty at every start; with the
      # admin panel disabled nothing ever writes it.
      CONFIG_FILE: "/run/vaultwarden/config.json"
    tmpfs:
      - /run/vaultwarden
    volumes:
      - vw_data:/data

  proxy:
    image: docker.io/library/caddy@sha256:003a97808e781aa9f7e75cc2f43d34d461099031faf5e20faefb9f61126836f0 # 2.11.9-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    configs:
      # The config name carries a revision that render.sh derives from this
      # whole file: docker compose keeps a running container when only the
      # inline content of a config changes, so without it an update would
      # measure the new Caddyfile and keep serving the old one (D-049).
      - source: caddyfile_98b31d481efb
        target: /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
    volumes:
      # caddy_data (persistent) keeps the ACME account, which a CAA
      # accounturi record can pin. Certificates and their PRIVATE KEYS go to
      # caddy_certs, a tmpfs: they exist in memory only and are gone when the
      # CVM stops. Whatever ran in this CVM before (the disk key depends on
      # the app id and the KMS, not on the compose) cannot have left a TLS
      # key behind, and nothing that runs later finds this one on disk.
      # Cost: a new certificate at every boot. Let's Encrypt allows 5
      # identical certificates per week, so more than 5 cold starts in a
      # week leave the service without a certificate until the limit refills.
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_certs:/data/caddy/certificates
      - caddy_config:/config

  attest:
    image: ghcr.io/facundomedica/attest-sidecar@sha256:00055017952f7eae1c2ef13aab762a682a5738cf7db559e5ffb5786bb4894463
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Root, with every capability dropped: Caddy writes its certificate
    # files 0600 root (directories 0700), so only uid 0 can read the leaf,
    # and the guest agent socket is root-only as well. The sidecar sees the
    # certificates tmpfs (read-only) and nothing else of Caddy's storage.
    user: "0:0"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    environment:
      ATTEST_PLATFORM: "dstack"
      ATTEST_LISTEN: "0.0.0.0:8081"
      ATTEST_CERT_PATH: "/certs/acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory/vault.facundo.dev/vault.facundo.dev.crt"
      ATTEST_DSTACK_SOCKET: "/var/run/dstack.sock"
    volumes:
      - caddy_certs:/certs:ro
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock

configs:
  caddyfile_98b31d481efb:
    content: |
      {
        admin off
      }
      vault.facundo.dev {
        # One pinned issuer, so the sidecar knows where the leaf lives.
        # TLS-ALPN-01 only: port 80 is not exposed.
        tls {
          issuer acme {
            dir https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
            disable_http_challenge
          }
        }
        handle /.well-known/tee-attestation {
          # Public evidence, no credentials: let a browser verifier page
          # on another origin fetch it.
          header Access-Control-Allow-Origin "*"
          reverse_proxy attest:8081
        }
        handle {
          reverse_proxy vaultwarden:80
        }
      }

volumes:
  vw_data:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:
  # In-memory only (see the proxy service). Mounted by proxy (rw) and attest
  # (ro); it lives as long as one of them runs.
  caddy_certs:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: tmpfs
      device: tmpfs
      o: "size=8m,mode=0700,nosuid,nodev,noexec"
pre_launch_script:
# Attested Vaultwarden pre-launch script, part 1: start from the measured
# compose only (measured: part of app-compose; pinned by the policy's
# pre_launch_script_sha256).
#
# dstack `source`s the pre-launch script from app-compose.sh under
# `set -euo pipefail`, then runs `docker compose up -d` on the measured
# compose. Docker's state (containers, networks, the files compose
# materialises for inline `configs`) lives on the persistent data disk and
# is NOT measured. `docker compose up` reuses a container whose service
# definition it considers unchanged, and dstack passes no --force-recreate.
# Seen live: after a compose update that changed only the inline Caddyfile,
# the proxy container was kept and Caddy went on serving the OLD
# configuration while RTMR3 held the NEW compose hash.
#
# So before compose runs, remove every container (with its anonymous
# volumes) and every unused network. Named volumes are kept: they hold the
# data. Every container is then created from the measured compose on this
# boot. A failure here aborts the boot (fail closed).
#
# This does not make the persistent disk trustworthy: a non-published
# compose that ran earlier under the same app id could have changed the
# image store or the named volumes (docs/THREAT_MODEL.md section 1).
avw_leftover="$(docker ps -aq)"
if [ -n "$avw_leftover" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word splitting intended: one id per word
  docker rm -f -v $avw_leftover
fi
docker network prune -f
if [ -n "$(docker ps -aq)" ]; then
  echo "pre-launch: containers left after cleanup, refusing to start" >&2
  exit 1
fi
unset avw_leftover
# Attested Vaultwarden pre-launch script (measured: part of app-compose).
#
# dstack `source`s this from app-compose.sh under `set -euo pipefail`, with
# the decrypted env in the environment. It logs in to GHCR so the private,
# digest-pinned sidecar image can be pulled.
#
# Only the token comes from encrypted env (unmeasured); registry and user are
# fixed here. A substituted token cannot change which image runs: every image
# is pinned by @sha256 digest, so a wrong token only makes the pull fail.
#
# The root filesystem is read-only (dm-verity), so docker's credential store
# goes to /tmp, as in Phala's default script. The export reaches the
# `docker compose up` that app-compose.sh runs next in the same shell.
export DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/.docker
mkdir -p "$DOCKER_CONFIG"
chmod 700 "$DOCKER_CONFIG"
printf '%s' "${GHCR_READ_TOKEN:?GHCR_READ_TOKEN is not set}" \
  | docker login ghcr.io --username facundomedica --password-stdin
